newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: SUPPORT FOR SACKED PNG DEFENCE CHIEF
The sacked commander of the PNG defence force, Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok, has received support from a senior PNG army officer, and the leader of the Bouganville Revolutionary Army.
The commander was dismissed yesterday after giving the Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan, and senior government ministers, 48-hours to resign over plans to use foreign mercenaries on Bougainville.

Operations officer for the current operation in Port Moresby, Major Walter Enuma, says the standoff with the government is only over the hiring of mercenaries from the British based company, Sandline International.

Meanwhile, leader of the Bouganville Revolutionary Army, Francis Ona, has thrown his support behind the sacked defence chief, saying General Singirok would be more likely to negotiate with him than Prime Minister, Julius Chan.
REPORT INTO COLSTON TO BE TABLED TODAY
The Federal Opposition expects that the report into allegations against Independent Senator, Mal Colston will be tabled in the Senate today.
Senator Colston and Senate President, Margaret Reid, asked Senate officials to prepare the report when allegations were made that Senator Colston had misused his travel entitlements.
Senator Colston has given Senator Reid his response, and it's expected that will be tabled when the report is revealed.
There's also a separate report being prepared by the Department of Administrative Services into other allegations against Senator Colston.
He's denied all the allegations.
REWARD ANNOUNCED FOR INFORMATION ON SERIAL KILLER
Police in Perth say the posting of a 250-thousand dollar reward for information leading to the capture of a serial killer preying on young women has prompted a flood of calls from the public.
The West Autralian Government offered the reward yesterday for information leading to the whereabouts of Sarah Spiers and Ciara Glennon, and the person responsible for the murder of Jane Rimmer.
All three women vanished from the Claremont nightstrip in the past 15 months.
Ms Glennon, a 27-year-old lawyer, has been missing for three days.
The body of 23-year-old Jane Rimmer was found in bush south of Perth last August, two months after she disappeared.
Eighteen year-old Sarah Spiers has been missing for 15 months.
LEGAL ACTION OVER CARMEN LAWRENCE'S LEGAL BILL
Legal action has started in the Federal Court in Sydney over a legal bill of former Federal Health minister Carmen Lawrence.
The law firm, Dunhill Madden Butler, is trying to recover money from the Commonwealth after representing the Labor MP at the 1995 Marks Royal Commission.
After a brief mention today, Justice Davies adjourned the matter until May.
The Royal Commission was established in May 1995 to examine Doctor Lawrence's knowledge of a petition filed in the West Australian Legislative Council in 1992.
EASTMAN SACKS APPEAL SOLICITOR
The man convicted of murdering Federal Police Assistant Commissioner Colin Winchester, is now conducting his own appeal after this morning sacking his solicitor.
51-year-old David Harold Eastman sacked solicitor Bernard Collaery, saying his action was not a criticism of Mr Collaery, as Mr Collaery had been providing his services for free for eight weeks.
But he said Mr Collaery also had a business to run and as a result could not devote adequate time to the appeal.
Before being dismissed, Mr Collaery told the Federal Court that Legal Aid funding for the retention of Eastman's barristers had run out, which would limit their appearances.
ARCHIBALD PRIZE TO BE ANNOUNCED FRIDAY
The winner of this year's Archibald Prize will be announced at the Art Gallery of New South Wales on Friday.
Portraits of former Australian of the year Dr John Yu, writer Peter Carey and singer Tex Perkins are among entries chosen to hang in this year's exhibition.
There are more than 480 entries, with 31 chosen for exhibition.

Among the artists selected: Fred Cress, who's painted David Williamson, Joe Furlonger with a self portrait, Bill Leak with a painting of Tex Perkins, Tim Shultz with Wendy Sharpe, Martin Sharp with Tiny Tim, Judy Cassab with Elwyn Lynn, Nigel Thomson with Barbara Blackman, Paul Newton with Kate Fischer and Barbie, and Adam Cullen's portrait of Mikey Robbins.
The Wynne, Sulman and Dobell prizes will also be announced on Friday.
STRIKE HAS IMPACT ON NSW WAITING LISTS
The New South Wales Health Minister, Andrew Refshauge, says waiting lists have grown by thousands as a result of the week-long strike by junior doctors.
The doctors are in dispute with the Federal Government over it's decision to limit the provision of Medicare provider numbers to the junior doctors.
Last night, they agreed to an offer of a meeting with Health minister, Dr Michael Wooldridge, and will end their industrial action tomorrow.
Dr Refshauge says he's relieved because the strike was having a significant impact on the state's already stretched health system.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
